stories.title: Rust 2024 Edition: What's New and Why It Matters
stories.tldr: The Rust 2024 Edition brings cleaner async syntax, improved ergonomics for pattern matching, and several long-awaited language stabilizations.

stories.title: This Week in Rust 553: New async trait stabilization, embedded targets, and community news
stories.tldr: This week's digest covers the stabilization of async traits in nightly, new embedded target support, and highlights from the Rust community forums.

stories.title: Async Rust Is A Bad Language — A Counterpoint
stories.tldr: A rebuttal arguing that async Rust's complexity is a fair trade-off for its correctness guarantees, and that the ecosystem has matured significantly.

stories.title: Announcing Rust 1.80.0: LazyCell and LazyLock reach stable
stories.tldr: Rust 1.80 stabilizes LazyCell and LazyLock for zero-cost lazy initialization, pattern restrictions, and numerous compiler performance improvements.

stories.title: Rewriting NGINX in Rust: Performance Lessons from Pingora
stories.tldr: Cloudflare's Pingora handles more than 1 trillion requests per day and uses 70% less CPU than its NGINX predecessor thanks to Rust's zero-cost abstractions.

stories.title: I wrote my first production Rust service — here's what I learned
stories.tldr: A developer shares their journey from Python to Rust for a high-throughput data pipeline, noting that the borrow checker caught real production bugs during development.

stories.title: Rust's borrow checker explained with animated diagrams
stories.tldr: An interactive guide using animated SVG diagrams to demystify Rust's borrow checker, lifetimes, and ownership model for newcomers.

stories.title: Are We Game Yet? — August 2026 update: Bevy 0.14 and the ecosystem
stories.tldr: Bevy 0.14 ships with a new retained rendering architecture, improved ECS scheduling, and a redesigned asset pipeline that simplifies game development in Rust.

stories.title: Tokio 1.40 released: improved metrics, task names, and runtime tracing
stories.tldr: Tokio 1.40 introduces named tasks for better debugging, built-in metrics for Prometheus, and a tracing integration that surfaces runtime bottlenecks automatically.

stories.title: Inside Rust: Progress on the parallel front-end compiler
stories.tldr: The Rust compiler team shares benchmarks showing 30-50% faster incremental compile times with the parallel front-end, now available on nightly behind a feature flag.
